Name: Incomplete Data/State Propagation
Description:
The product passes control to another component
	  or function, or it performs a state transition, but it does
	  not provide some security-critical data/state that is needed
	  by the receiving component/function.

CommonConsequences.Note: The consequences will vary depending on the type of data/state that is omitted, along with the functionality that the data/state supports.
If the data/state is needed for a security decision, such as authentication or authorization, then this could allow attackers to bypass the intended protection mechanism.

MappingNotes.Rationale: This CWE Entry is a Class and might have lower-level children that would be more appropriate
MappingNotes.Comments: Examine children of this entry to see if there is a better fit

ObservedExamples.Description: Chain: File archive product for Windows does not preserve Mark-of-the-Web (MOTW) when extracting an archive (CWE-1475) due to incorrect matching (CWE-697) and canonicalization.
File archive product for Windows does not propagate the Zone.Identifier alternate data stream to extracted files, allowing a Mark-of-the-Web (MOTW) bypass.
Chain: Identity service does not propagate an expiry for a token (CWE-1475), allowing attackers to bypass intended token lifetime restrictions (CWE-863).

PotentialMitigations.Description: Clearly identify security-critical data/state structures and ensure that they are propagated when necessary. Be careful of error conditions that could redirect control flow in a way that prevents the propagation from occurring.
